changed.title: At most 500k·2^max(19,⌊k/2⌋) AND/OR/NOT gates of fan-in at most two for the three-round key test on two k-bit names, k ≥ 20
changed.statement:
∀ k : Nat, 20 ≤ k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range 3).foldl (fun state i =>
      step (state ^^^ rot 1 state ^^^ rot (k - 1) state) ^^^
        rot (2 * i) rowKey ^^^ constant (i + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range 3).foldl (fun state i =>
      step (state ^^^ rot 2 state ^^^ rot (k - 2) state) ^^^
        rot (3 * (i + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (3 + (i + 1))) (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let low := k - (k + 1) / 2
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < 2 ^ low) && decide (second w col.val < 2 ^ low))
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2 ^ max 19 low * (500 * k) ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits
changed.unlocks: a ceiling for the candidate rule cut to three rounds, the one round count the row-side slots cannot do, for the line that says which round counts are cheap
changed.context: On paper. Put z = rot3(w) xor v. Fix 19 seed bits and every bit left outside the sweep. Descend through the top h column equations. At bit i the state term reads only z[i-6..i+12]. The key contributes z[i-7] alone. Wire a fresh pivot from that equation, or compare it with its seed bit on a wrap. Recover w from z and v, test the row on w and u, then OR all accepting slots. Count 815 gates per pivot computation, five per comparison and 65k for key recovery and the row rounds. The total fits 500k gates per slot including joins.

changed.title: Five-input monotone f with table 0xeae8e880: some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 9 gates computes f
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ ∀ x : Fin 5 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = Nat.testBit 0xeae8e880 (∑ i : Fin 5, if x i then 2 ^ (i : ℕ) else 0)
changed.unlocks: settles the least AND/OR size of this five-input monotone function at 9; with the checked row that NOT gates save nothing on it, also its least AND/OR/NOT size
changed.context: FIND (beat this). The answer is an object, not an argument: give the gate list (AND/OR, at most two inputs each, at most 9 gates) and decide the equality over all 32 inputs. The best circuit known to us has 10 gates; none with 8 or fewer exists (exhaustive search, computed, not checked); whether 9 is possible is unknown to us. Pattern: methods/find/example-maj3.lean.txt.
changed.sketch: f on five inputs is true when some listed set is all true: 012, 013, 023, 123, 014, 024, 124, 034 (at least three of 0..3, or 4 with two of 0, 1, 2, or 4 with 0 and 3). We hold a 10-gate AND/OR circuit; an exhaustive search of ours found none with 8 or fewer (computed), so 9 is the only open size. Step: give 9 AND or OR gates, fan-in at most two, each reading only earlier wires, output last; judged by evaluating on all 32 inputs against the table, by decide. A hand idea: share the pair products of 0, 1, 2 between the three-of-four part and the part with 4.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: on every nonfull column an AND operand tells two row neighborhoods apart, for a graph represented by an AND/OR circuit
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (u v : Fin n)
    (j : Fin C.gates.length) (q : ℕ),
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let g := n + m + j.val
  let edge := fun source target : ℕ => ∃ idx : Fin C.gates.length,
    target = n + m + idx.val ∧ source ∈ (gate idx.val).inputs
  let cuts := fun (z start : ℕ) =>
    ¬ (start ≠ z ∧ C.output ≠ z ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun prev next : ℕ => prev ≠ z ∧ next ≠ z ∧ edge prev next) start C.output)
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → u ≠ v →
  (gate j.val).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and →
  q ∈ (gate j.val).inputs →
  cuts g u.val → cuts q v.val → ¬ Relation.ReflTransGen edge u.val q →
  ∀ c : Fin m, (∃ w : Fin n, G w c = false) →
    let col := List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun b : Fin m => decide (b = c))
    let value := (C.wires col).getD q false
    (G u c = true → value = true) ∧ (G v c = true → value = false)
changed.unlocks: one step of the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise, which pins an AND operand at a column alone; it rests on the checked domination row and moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. With only the column on, the output is off by monotonicity against a row that misses it. When adding a row changes the output, trace changed operands back to that input. For row u this path crosses the AND, so its operand q is on. Row u has no path to q, so q was on at the column alone. For row v the changed path crosses q itself. Adding the row can only turn q on, so q was off at the column alone.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 39262 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 10 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (39262 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 10
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 11 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 10; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.
